card.title: Gas laws — Boyle and Charles fuse into PV = nRT

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Boyle (P∝1/V at fixed T), Charles (V∝T at fixed P) and Avogadro (V∝n) each freeze two variables and watch the third — multiply all three proportionalities and the combined law (P₁V₁/T₁ = P₂V₂/T₂) appears, with R crowning it as PV = nRT. Dalton splits mixture pressures by mole fraction; Graham sorts diffusion speeds by 1/√M. Liquids add vapour pressure/boiling/surface tension/viscosity; solids add lattices, unit cells and water of crystallization.

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: Boyle: P₁V₁ = P₂V₂ · Charles: V₁/T₁ = V₂/T₂ (kelvin!) · combined: P₁V₁/T₁ = P₂V₂/T₂ · PV = nRT · Dalton: P_total = ΣPᵢ, Pᵢ = xᵢ·P  ·  Graham: r₁/r₂ = √(M₂/M₁)  ·  500 cm³ at 27 °C → 127 °C, same P: V = 500×400/300 ≈ 667 cm³

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Charles and the combined law demand KELVIN — Celsius silently breaks them. Gas laws assume ideal behaviour (low P, high T); real gases deviate via molecular volume and attractions (van der Waals). Dalton needs non-reacting components; Graham needs same T and P for both gases.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: 500 cm³ at 27 °C (300 K) → 127 °C (400 K), constant P: V₂ = 500 × 400/300 ≈ 667 cm³ (NEB 2021). Efflorescent salts lose water to air, deliquescent dissolve in absorbed water, hygroscopic merely attract it. Liquid crystals flow like liquids but order like solids (LCDs).

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: State Boyle (V∝1/P) and Charles (V∝T), then fuse: V ∝ T/P → PV/T = constant = nR for n moles → PV = nRT, with R = 8.314 J/mol·K the bridge between the gas world and energy (NEB 2023, 3 marks). Derivation beats memorisation — three laws, one product.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Ideal equations fail near condensation (high P, low T) — liquefaction is the visible rebellion. Viscosity/surface-tension pictures here are qualitative only (syllabus says so). Unit-cell counting assumes perfect crystals; defects run the real semiconductor world.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: Combine: V ∝ 1/P (Boyle) and V ∝ T (Charles) and V ∝ n (Avogadro) → V = R·nT/P. Dalton: each gas exerts its mole-fraction share, Pᵢ = xᵢP, proved by applying PV = nRT per component in the shared V, T. Graham: equal KE (½mv²) at same T → v ∝ 1/√m → diffusion rates follow.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Temperature to kelvin FIRST — every year someone loses marks on 27 °C. Combined-law ladder: cross-multiply P₁V₁T₂ = P₂V₂T₁. Graham: lighter diffuses faster by √mass-ratio. R = 8.314 pairs with joules/m³; R = 0.0821 with L·atm.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: NEB 2023 (3): Boyle + Charles → derive ideal gas equation. NEB 2021 (2): 500 cm³ at 27 °C → volume at 127 °C, constant P. Dalton/Graham and liquid/solid-state definitions rotate yearly.
